newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN warns Portugal on Timor, backs Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN warns Portugal on Timor, backs Indonesia.

text.p: ASEAN leaders warned Portugal on Saturday against making Indonesia's rule in East Timor an issue between the seven-nation Southeast Asian grouping and the European Union.

A joint statement at the end of a one-day ASEAN summit said one EU member could aggravate ties by "introducing extraneous issues such as the question of East Timor in the economic cooperation and interaction between ASEAN and the EU".
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said this referred to Portugal and added that while Lisbon's efforts had failed, they were becoming an increasingly irritating factor in their relations.
He said ASEAN leaders had reiterated their full support for Indonesia's position on East Timor.

"Portugal has failed to achieve its purpose and ambition, but it is aggravating the relationship between ASEAN and the EU," he said after the summit attended by leaders from Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and declared the territory its 27th province the following year, in a move unrecognised by the United Nations, which considers Lisbon the administering authority.
A gathering of human rights activists over East Timor in the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur earlier this month was disrupted by a band of pro-government Malaysian youths.

Manila also banned self-exiled East Timorese anti-Indonesian activist Jose Ramos Horta, joint recipient of the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize, from the Philippines during the recent Asian- Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum to prevent possible disruptions during the visit by leaders of the 18 APEC members.

Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad told a news conference after Saturday's ASEAN summit he hoped neither the EU nor ASEAN would be forced to discuss matters that should not be discussed by them.
"A dialogue can only be held if both sides agree there should be a dialogue. If one side imposes a condition on the other, of course there may not be a dialogue," he said.
"I do hope people will not make it difficult for us to have a dialogue, because the dialogue could be useful," he said.

In their joint statement, ASEAN leaders said that Portugal's actions could also jeopardise tripartite talks on East Timor currently taking place between Portugal and Indonesia under the auspices of the United Nations.

"The heads of government reiterated their full support for the Indonesian position on East Timor and rejected the introduction of such an extraneous issue into ASEAN-EU relations by a certain member of the EU," the statement said.
Indonesia's Alatas said Portugal had tried to make East Timor a condition in ASEAN-EU relations. "This only unwarrantedly and unnecessarily aggravates the relationship."
"Indonesia raised the issue and got the support of all other heads of government of ASEAN," he added.
